canaries.name: keep_plaintext_on_fail
canaries.note: Presented as skipping a memset on the failure path that 'callers discard anyway'; a forged message now leaves its unauthenticated decryption in the caller's buffer.

canaries.name: drop_full_block_flag
canaries.note: Presented as dropping a domain-separation term that is 'always zero' (leftover >> 4); it is one exactly when the last block is full, so hashes of messages whose length is a positive multiple of 16 change, and such a message now collides with its 15-byte-shorter prefix padded with 0x80. Tests only pin hashes of other lengths.

canaries.name: xor128_u128
canaries.note: Presented as a faster 128-bit xor (one u128 load, xor and store instead of a byte loop); LLVM already vectorizes the byte loop, and the hash workload runs slightly more instructions.

candidates.name: rolled_rounds
candidates.note: Xoodoo.permute runs its 12 rounds as a runtime loop over the round constants instead of an inline for that the compiler fully unrolls, so programs carry one copy of the round instead of twelve. Output is unchanged; the trade is speed (the ReleaseFast workloads run about 11 to 13 percent more instructions, measured before writing this note), which is what a size-first build of a library for memory-constrained devices asks for.
